info.title: KeyClerk API
info.description: Everything a KeyClerk front end can see and do. Reads are views over the records, filtered by who asks; writes are change requests that the engine applies, holds for a second key, or refuses with reasons. A browser session (cookie) sends the CSRF token from /me in the X-KeyClerk-CSRF header on every POST; a front end with its own broker client sends a bearer token from an allowed client. Errors share one shape.

x-meanings.unauthenticated: not signed in, or the bearer token is not valid here
x-meanings.forbidden: signed in, but this view or action is not yours
x-meanings.not_found: no such call, group, person or change
x-meanings.refused: the desk or the engine said no; the message says why
x-meanings.invalid: the request does not match the contract
x-meanings.busy: every worker is busy; try again shortly
x-meanings.csrf: a browser session must send X-KeyClerk-CSRF from /me, from this site
x-meanings.not_allowed: this method is not offered on this path
x-meanings.rate_limited: too many requests from one person: 30 changes in 10 minutes, 4 requests at once
x-meanings.internal: a fault on the server; nothing was changed by it

Request_confirm_guest.description: Confirm the guest is with you (the host or organiser), before the timer suspends them

attendee.description: an anchor, a name, or unregistered with a label

Request_add_attendee.description: Add someone not on the list (the host, the organiser or the front office)

kind.description: visitor (escorted) or RESTRICTED (a second person signs)

until.description: when it ends; never after the visit closes

Request_return_badge.description: Record that a badge was handed back (the front office)

custodians.description: the people break-glass halves may be escrowed to (at least two)

unlock_key.description: the edge node's P-256 public key for phoned unlock (kc-unlock-v2), uncompressed SEC1, base64url; in its TPM where it has one

unlock_approvers.description: who may read an unlock code (never the person unlocked)

statement.description: the kc-edge-officer-v2 statement (purpose enrolment: edge, officer, officer key, the node's enrolment key, unlock key and TPM commitment), signed over the same bytes by the officer and by the edge (amendment 0014d)

targets.description: the bastion targets, each with the role it grants and the entitlement that leads to it

Request_enrol_edge.description: Enrol an edge (the root; waits for the security officer's key)

public_key.description: the X25519 public key derived from your passkey through PRF, base64url

ssh_key.description: the ssh-ed25519 public key your hardware key holds

credential_id.description: the WebAuthn credential id the key came from

user_verification.description: the authenticator verified you (PIN or biometric)

attestation.description: the attestation format the authenticator gave, if any

Request_enrol_person_key.description: Register your hardware key (yourself; waits for a second key)

hours.description: the window, at most what edge.rego and the ceiling allow

Request_grant_visit_lease.description: Grant a visit lease on an assured edge (waits for a second key)

enrolment_key.description: the edge's new (or same) enrolment key

unlock_key.description: the edge node's P-256 public key for phoned unlock (kc-unlock-v2), uncompressed SEC1, base64url; in its TPM where it has one

statement.description: the kc-edge-officer-v2 statement with purpose rotation, signed by the (new) officer and the edge's (new) enrolment key

Request_rotate_edge.description: Rotate an edge's enrolment key or officer (waits for the security officer's key)

id.description: an edge, a person key or a visit lease

Request_end_edge_record.description: End an edge, a person key or a visit lease

bearer.bearerFormat: JWT (RS256, from the broker; azp an allowed client)
